cells.place: No. 3. Findspot: Do.
cells.date: Regnal year 488, Regnal year 11, Kārtika śu. 8.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the ruler and registers the royal gift of two nivartanas of land at Embalāḍa made to a vihāra by the queen Paramabhaṭṭārikā-mahādēvī, for the enjoyment of the Arya-sangha-bhikshus visiting the place from all the four quarters. The queen is stated to belong to the family of the Prithivimūlas. Towards the end of the charter it is stated that Uttamaśraya, on obtaining some success-ful expedition against the Pallava king Sinha, made the gift. The charter ends with a stanza in praise of the king Mūla-rāja. In characters of the 6th century A.D. Published in ibid., Vol. 42, part 7, pp. 7 ff., and plates.

cells.date: Śaka 794, Regnal year Khara, Kārttika śu. 15, solar eclipse, Rohiṇī, Wednesday. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Contains the genealogical account of the dynasty. Mentions the conquests of Subhatunga (Khamber), ruling over Gaṅga-mandala. Records that the king, while he was encamped at the village of Tesimi-snigdhal-grāma, made a grant of that village to the brāhmaṇa Madiāva, alias Bhaimāyavamma, son of Vāmanabhaṭṭa and grandson of the prince. Also records the grant of the village Gotte-madi by Brahmavira-vallabha to the Rājasabhā at Talavana-pura in which he had installed (an image) of Bhagavatī. The record was written by Vivakarmāchārya, an expert in fine arts.

cells.dynasty: Chandra of B. E. ŚrīChandra Bengal.
cells.remarks: Issued from Vikramapura. Contains a genealogical account of the dynasty. States that the śākhika state of Pañchala-grama (Pauṇḍra-vardhana-bhukti) was separated to Skandatavaroga, all situated in Schratta-maṇdala in Pauṇḍra-vardhana-bhukti, were constituted into a brāhmaṇapura named Śrīchandrapura after the king. Records a number of donations to the deities (such as Yamaleśvara-bhaṭṭāraka and Mahākāla of the Deśāntariyas and Vaṅgāla mathas) and to 6000 brāhmaṇas of whom only thirty-seven are named. The grant was made on the occasion of Śrāvaṇa-Ravi-saṁkrānti. The dhlātaka was written by Sūtradhāra Śrī-Śivachandra and engraved by the artisan Haridāsa. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXVII, pp. 280 ff., and plates.

cells.place:
Tiṟunallār.—Darbbāṇyēśvara temple, Chōla
Ṛāfamanḍapa, north wall, outside.
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Commences with the praśasti, Pūmanniyē-danam etc. Purports to be a memorandum declaring some lands as dēvadāna in the temple in the 40th year of the revenue register as brāhmaṇōttama Tirumallālam, issued by the king at the instance of Vikramasōlak-kāyāyar to provide for the expenses for conducting the affairs of the temple of god Tirunallārudaiyār in Tirunallāru alias Virudarājabhayaṅkara-nāḍu, a subdivision of Jayakoṇḍaśōla-vaḻanāḍu. It is said that the existing dēvadāna lands of the temple proved to be insufficient to meet the expenses and to pay taxes to the king's treasury. Some transactions of the 38th and the 43th years, probably, in the reign of Kulōttuṅga I are referred to.

cells.place: Tiṟunallār.—Darbbāṇyēśvara temple, Chōla Ṛāfamanḍapa, north wall, outside. Vari and tripatta †
cells.remarks: Partly built in. Records an order granting lands to the temple of Tirumūlavar and Māṇikkam at Muḷaiyūr in the guṇḍolā-vaḷanāḍu as tax-free devadāna for residential quarters around the temple, for a road for the deity's sea-bath (kaḍalāḍu tirunīḍi) and also for flower-gardens named after Kulaśēkhara-sūri and Sundara-śōla-sūrikarai. Refers to the land-survey conducted during the 10th year of Suigaṇṭavār-kuḷa (i.e., Kulōttuṅga I) and to some settlements made in the 19th and the 39th years perhaps of the same king. The grant of 10th day in the 5th year of the king signed by the officer Ūttattiruv-arari is also given. In characters of about the 12th century.

cells.place: Chaṇḍēśvara shrine in Darbbāṇyēśvara temple, walls. †
cells.date: Regnal year 25+1, Tulā śu, 10, Sādayam, Wednesday=1241 A.D., October 10.
cells.remarks: Records the assignment of lands as tirunāmattukkāṇi after purchase from Chōtamaṇi-Perumān of Avvaivaḷḷūr out of the money realised from the Sivabrāhmaṇas on account of their failure to contribute rice, parched rice, gingelly oil and māṇ-eṇṇai probably in respect of a previous endowment, by the manager (ūniyār) of the temple, Kaṇḍan Tiruchchirrambalam for the temple and the Nāḷvār of Muḷaiyūr-nāḍu, who assembled for the purpose in the Nāḍuvai-nāyakan-tirumaṇḍapam in the temple. The representatives of the groups which met such as Sarabāṇam, Tirukkaikotti, Timvil-Aṅdārar, etc., have signed the record.

cells.place: Tripatta in the north side
cells.remarks: Sōlakēra-maṇḍalam. It is stated that the survey was made with a linear measure (kōl), 12 aḍi and 1 riakkadi long, and that the land so measured will be reckoned at the rate of one ma for each kōl. The date is given as Saka 1458, Durmukha. There are two plus marks flanking the inscription, and under the right hand side mark are three lines of writing stating that this is the measurement of the kōl.

cells.place: First prākāra, left of entrance, inside
cells.remarks: Records an undertaking by the ūrār of Kiraṇūr in Vaḍaśīru-vāyi-nāḍu in Jayasiṅgakulakāla vaḷanāḍu they agree to refrain from damaging tanks, trees and wells in the prākāra, held by the temple in the course of a strife among themselves. cells.location: Dēsan, former Dungarpur State.
cells.date:
(1) Vikrama 1453, Śaka 1318, Kārttika ba. 7, Monday, Rōhiṇī=1396 A.D., October 23. (The date for śu. 2 was, however, Pushya).
(2) Vikrama 1520, Śaka 1486, Vaiśākha śu. 3, Monday, Rōhiṇī=1464 A.D., April 9.
cells.remarks: Records the consecration of a well by Maṅkāde, wife of Rāula Karmasiṁha, son of Duṅgarasiṁha and grandson of Chuṇḍa, on the first date, States that on the second date, the well was renovated by Dhikāka, son of Muktāde, wife of Rāula Joṇasasiṁha (Joṇaśrasiṁha). The record was written by Druva-maharahi of Mēdāpāṭa-jñāti and was perhaps engraved by sūtradhāra Gigāka.

cells.date: Vikrama 1218, Āśvina śu. 1, Thursday = 1161 A.D., September 21.
cells.remarks: Badly damaged. Gives the genealogy of the Paramāras of Kīrātākūpa who were the feudatories of the Chālukyas and mentions Sōmeśvara, and records that the latter captured two forts of the king Jajjaka and took 1700 horses from him. The praśasti was composed by Narasimha, written by Yaśōdēva and engraved by the mason Jajja,la. Published in Poona Orientalist, Vol. I, No. II, pp. 47 ff.; Bhandarkar's List, No. 312.

cells.date: Vikrama 1557, Vaiśākha śu. 6, Friday, Punarvasu= 1501 A.D., April 28.
cells.remarks: Narrates the pattāvalī of Saṁdēva-gachchha founded by Yaśō- bhadra-sūri and also gives the genealogy of the ruler. Records the construction of the maṇḍapa of the Ādinātha temple along with their families, of the ihaukikā which was built at Naṁdakulavati (i.e., Nīdlī) in Vikrama 964 by Bhānu- Sāyara and the installation of the image of Ādiśvara, in the Jina-vasati by Iśvara-sūri of the Śāntisūri-patṭa on the orders of Mahārājādhirāja Rāyamalla of the Guhila family; written by āchārya Iśvara-sūri and engraved by sūtrādhāra Śōmāka. Transcribed in Jaina Inscriptions, Part I, pp. 215 ff.; Bhandarkar's List, No. 874.

cells.location: Chinna (Chikoti) Mangalāram
cells.place: Loose slab lying on a grave,
cells.date: Shuhūr 1074 (words), A. H. 1084, Jumādā II 12=1673 A.D., September 14.
cells.remarks: Records the text of a royal farmān announcing to the muqaddams, the kulkarnis and the ryots of the village Mangalwāram, in the division (a mal) of Janwāra, alias Ḥasanābād that with the commencement of the Shuhūr year 1074 (1673 A.D.), the income from the village of Mangalwāram, was exclusively endowed for ever for the expenses of free-kitchen, the light, the reciters of the Qur'ān, and the attendants of the tomb of the late Neknām Khān, and further directing the office-bearers, the kārkuns, the desā'is, thalkaris, muqaddams and ryots, not to hinder or demand any tax or endowment for the said purpose without any hindrance. Ends with an imprescation against the violator. Cf. A. R. Arch. Dep. Niz. Dom., 1933-34, p. 7, f.n.1.

Inst., Vol. IV (1943), pp. 388-42.

cells.location: Dholkā
cells.place: Mosque in the Dargāh of Ḥaḍrat Shāh. Above the central miḥrāb.
cells.remarks: Refers to the endowment of the annual income from 189 villages included in the chalbandi of the qaṣba (town) of Dholkā, at the rate of one rupee from each, arranged in the time of Ghāzīkhān in the days of Shāh Jahān, to the mosque and the Khāngāh of Ḥaḍrat Shāh. It also states that 75 rupees were to be collected from the share of the Trustee and a quarter tanka from each of the merchants and the spot out of rent for the said establishment through Sher Miyān Parmār (a jāgīrdār of Dholkā). In characters of about the 19th century.
